subject: SIG follow-up: request for commit provenance manifest and CI artifact checksums
messages:
From: Michael Chen <m.chen@bluecrest.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: commit provenance manifest request

Irene —

Thanks again for the quick SIG intake yesterday. The assessor team asked for a concise export we can use for a focused review: a commit-provenance manifest covering PRs merged to main in the last six months (author, PR number, merge commit SHA, reviewer list, merge timestamp), plus the signed CI artifact checksums for those runs. If possible, include a short mapping to which CI job produced each artifact and the retention policy applied.

We need this in CSV or manifest JSON form; the assessor prefers CSV for quick loading. Targeting a delivery window: can your team provide a snapshot by EOD next business day? Our deadline for the SIG intake is end of next week.

Attached: the assessor's short request form for scope.

Best,
Michael
Michael Chen
Bluecrest Security — External Assessor

Attachment: sig_request_form.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <m.chen@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: commit provenance manifest request

Michael —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attached form. We can produce a CSV manifest with the fields you listed (author, PR#, merge SHA, reviewers, merge timestamp) plus a column for CI job name and artifact checksum. A few clarifying Qs before we start:

- Scope: confirm "last six months" means 2025-03-18 to 2025-09-18 (inclusive).
- Redaction: any PII or internal ticket IDs that must be removed prior to handoff? We will redact internal Jira IDs by default unless you request them.
- Signature: do you require signed (GPG) checksums or a signed statement from our build system? We can provide a build manifest with SHA256 checksums and a signed envelope from our CI signer.

Jordan and Marissa — looping you in to prepare the manifest and extract the CI artifact index. We expect to deliver a first snapshot within 48 hours; if the assessor needs a different format (JSON vs CSV) we can provide both.

Plan: Jordan will pull the PR/merge metadata and produce commit_manifest_sample.csv; Marissa will export the CI artifact index and checksums and note the retention/expiry window.

Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: initial_scope.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: commit provenance manifest request

Irene —

Working on this now. Quick notes on extraction approach so Bluecrest understands provenance:

1) PR + merge metadata: we’ll query the monorepo GraphQL endpoint and cross-check with Git tags. Fields exported: repo, path, PR number, author email, merge SHA, merge timestamp (UTC), reviewers (GitHub review approvals), and whether the PR was squash/merge/rebase.

2) CI artifact mapping: each build run generates artifacts stored in S3 with a run_id. I’ll include run_id and job_name, artifact_key, SHA256 checksum and the signed build envelope id (we sign envelopes with our ephemeral CI signer; signature id included).

3) Secrets handling: we cannot export raw credential material. For ephemeral/secrets sampling, we will include a redacted sampling log that shows which runner and steward accessed the ephemeral secret, plus the access window. If Bluecrest needs more detail we can produce a redaction guidance doc.

Attached: commit_manifest_sample.csv (header row + 10 sample rows) and ci-artifact-index.txt (compact index). These are samples; full extract will be ~50k rows.

Jordan Blake
Staff Engineer, Release infra
Redwood Inference

Attachments: commit_manifest_sample.csv (text/csv), ci-artifact-index.txt (text/plain)

From: Michael Chen <m.chen@bluecrest.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: commit provenance manifest request

Jordan / Irene —

Thanks for the quick sample. The assessor has two small follow-ups before we accept the snapshot:

1) Can you include the GPG-signed checksum file for the CI artifacts (or the CI envelope signature id mapped to a downloadable signature)? The assessor needs a verifiable signature for at least a 200-row random sample.

2) Add a reviewer_role column (indicating if reviewer was a designated code owner or ad-hoc reviewer) if that exists in your metadata — it helps the reviewer prioritize sampling.

Also, please include the retention policy reference (where you keep artifacts, TTL) and a short note about whether any artifacts were auto-pruned in the export window.

If you can provide those things by EOD today that would keep us on schedule.

- Michael
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <m.chen@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2025 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: commit provenance manifest request

Michael —

Confirmed, we will deliver the additional items you requested. Implementation notes / timeline:

• GPG-signed checksum envelope: Marissa will produce a signed checksum file for a 200-row random sample and provide the envelope id that maps to our CI signer (we will also include the SHA256 list for the full snapshot).
• reviewer_role: Jordan will augment the manifest export with reviewer_role where available (code-owner vs adhoc).
• retention policy: Marissa will attach our artifact lifecycle policy (short reference) and flag any artifacts that were pruned during the six-month window.

Deliverables and ETA: full CSV manifest + CI artifact index + signed sample checksum + retention policy reference by EOD today (2025-09-19). If the assessor needs formal redaction or a non-disclosure wrapper prior to delivery, let us know immediately and we will pause the export.

Next steps for Bluecrest: confirm whether you want internal ticket IDs redacted. If not, we will include them in a dedicated column.

Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (none)
